title: The K_x-orbit subset B(Σ)_x := K_x · A
body_html:
The $K_x$-orbit subset $\BSigma_x := K_x \cdot A$

Fix $x \in A$. Define $\hat K_x := \Fix_G(x)$ and $$\BSigma_x \;:=\; K_x \cdot A \;\subseteq\; \BSigma.$$

Lemma. $\BSigma_x = \hat K_x A = K_x M_x A = K_x \mathcal{B}(M) = \hat K_x \mathcal{B}(M)$.

The intermediate $M_x$ and $\mathcal{B}(M)$ refer to a Levi (or analogous) subgroup $M$ of $G$ relevant to the application — e.g. in §8 the Levi attached to a semisimple character. The role of $M$ is detailed separately in Plan: identify each connected component of B(Σ) as K_x · A task C.7 — TBD.
proof_html:
of $K_x \cdot A = \hat K_x \cdot A$ (= C.3.3)

This identifies $K_x \cdot A$ with the union of all apartments of $\BSigma$ through $x$ (combining with the geometric meaning of $\hat K_x \cdot A$ in Apartments of B(Σ): definition, Stab_G(A), and parametrization of apartments through x Corollary C.3.1').

Inclusion $\subseteq$. $K_x \subseteq \hat K_x$: every $k \in K_x$ fixes $x$ in $\BSigma$. Indeed $k \cdot x = [(k, x)]_\sim$ and $[(k, x)] = [(1, x)]$ iff $\exists n \in N$ with $n \cdot x = x$ (so $n \in \Fix_N(x)$, take $n = e$) and $k n \in K_x$ (i.e.\ $k \in K_x$, ✓). So $K_x \cdot A \subseteq \hat K_x \cdot A$.

Inclusion $\supseteq$. Take $\hat k \in \hat K_x$ and $a \in A$; construct $k' \in K_x$, $a' \in A$ with $\hat k \cdot a = k' \cdot a'$ in $\BSigma$.

By Sheaf7 Lemma lem:Stab_gx (= [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]]): $$\hat K_x \;=\; \Fix_G(x) \;=\; \Fix_N(x) \cdot K_x.$$

So write $\hat k = n k_0$ with $n \in \Fix_N(x)$ and $k_0 \in K_x$.

Set $$k' \;:=\; n k_0 n^{-1}, \qquad a' \;:=\; n \cdot a \;\in\; A.$$

  • $k' \in K_x$: by $N$-equivariance of the $K$-cosheaf, $n K_x n^{-1} = K_{nx} = K_x$ (since $n \cdot x = x$). So $n k_0 n^{-1} \in K_x$.
  • $a' \in A$: $N$ stabilises $A$ setwise.

We check $\hat k \cdot a = k' \cdot a'$ in $\BSigma$: $$\hat k \cdot a \;=\; [(\hat k, a)]_\sim \;=\; [(n k_0, a)]_\sim, \qquad k' \cdot a' \;=\; [(k', a')]_\sim \;=\; [(n k_0 n^{-1}, n a)]_\sim.$$

We verify the equivalence $(n k_0, a) \sim (n k_0 n^{-1}, n a)$ using $m := n \in N$:

  • $m \cdot a = n \cdot a = a'$, ✓.
  • $(n k_0)^{-1} \cdot (n k_0 n^{-1}) \cdot m = k_0^{-1} n^{-1} \cdot n k_0 n^{-1} \cdot n = k_0^{-1} k_0 n^{-1} n = 1 \in K_a$. ✓

So $(nk_0, a) \sim (n k_0 n^{-1}, na)$, i.e.\ $\hat k \cdot a = k' \cdot a'$ in $\BSigma$. Hence $\hat K_x \cdot A \subseteq K_x \cdot A$.

Combining the two inclusions: $K_x \cdot A = \hat K_x \cdot A$. $\square$

Geometric meaning

Combined with Apartments of B(Σ): definition, Stab_G(A), and parametrization of apartments through x Cor. C.3.1': $$\BSigma_x \;=\; K_x \cdot A \;=\; \hat K_x \cdot A \;=\; \bigcup_{A' \in \mathrm{Apt}_x} A' \;=\; \text{union of all apartments of } \BSigma \text{ through } x.$$

This is the precise geometric content of "$K_x$-stable neighborhood": $\BSigma_x$ is the closed star of $x$ at the apartment level.

The other equalities $K_x M_x A = K_x \mathcal{B}(M) = \hat K_x \mathcal{B}(M)$

These require specifying the Levi $M$ and using the Bruhat–Tits building $\mathcal{B}(M)$. The argument is application-dependent (e.g.\ §8 uses the Levi attached to a semisimple character $\phi$). The identifications follow by:

  • $M_x A = \mathcal{B}(M)$: standard building axiom for $\mathcal{B}(M)$ ($M$-apartments through $x$ cover $\mathcal{B}(M)$).
  • $K_x M_x A = K_x \mathcal{B}(M)$: substitution.
  • $K_x \mathcal{B}(M) = \hat K_x \mathcal{B}(M)$: same argument as $K_x A = \hat K_x A$ above, with $A$ replaced by $\mathcal{B}(M)$.

Detailed write-up of these deferred to task C.7 (Plan: identify each connected component of B(Σ) as K_x · A).

Downstream uses

This $K_x$-stable neighborhood is the home of the contraction extension [[node:building.contraction_extension_K3]] and of the supports of the $\phi_x$-isotypic chains studied in [[node:coefficient_systems.support_in_BSx]].

Combined with the building axiom (A1) inside a component ([[node:building.A1_axiom_in_component]]), this gives the main geometric identification $C_0 = K_x \cdot A$ in [[node:building.component_is_KxA]] (task C.3.4).
